ADDIS ABABA – Rwanda has presented its community-based health insurance scheme and its response to the 2024 Marburg outbreak as lessons for African countries seeking to reduce dependence on foreign health assistance.

As the continent faces growing pressure to finance its own healthcare systems, Prime Minister Dr Justin Nsengiyumva addressed the Fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) in Addis Ababa and offered Rwanda’s lessons.

Speaking on behalf of President Paul Kagame, who is the African Union Champion for Domestic Health Financing, Nsengiyumva demonstrated how Rwanda’s experience could help other African countries protect their populations when external support becomes less predictable.

“Reducing dependence on foreign assistance does not mean abandoning international partnerships, but ensuring African countries set their own priorities and lead implementation. We can no longer rely on others to meet our most fundamental health needs.” he told delegates.

Nsengiyumva explained that domestic financing, community-level healthcare and investment in preparedness is not about turning away from partnership.

It is about new partnership, he said, where Africa sets the priorities and leads implementation, with external financing aligned behind those priorities.

Mutuelle De Santé and The Question of Who Pays

Nsengiyumva cited Mutuelle de Santé, Rwanda’s community-based health insurance scheme, as an example of how domestic solutions can widen access to healthcare.

Over 25 years, the scheme has extended coverage to about 89 per cent of Rwandans, improving access to essential medicines and specialized treatment. He linked this progress to improvements in the country’s health indicators.

Since 2000, infant deaths have fallen from 107 to 27 per 1,000 live births, while maternal deaths have declined from 1,071 to 149 per 100,000 live births. Life expectancy has increased from about 50 to 70.5 years.

He attributed these gains to investments in health workers, digitalization and infrastructure, alongside the insurance scheme, which has helped families access care they might otherwise struggle to afford.

However, expanding coverage has also created pressure to sustain the scheme financially. Nsengiyumva acknowledged that its original structure became increasingly difficult to maintain as the burden fell disproportionately on Government.

Rwanda introduced an income-based contribution framework in 2026, requiring people with greater financial means to contribute more while the poorest receive full Government subsidies.

The Prime Minister said members now account for 37 per cent of the scheme’s financing, with Government and the private sector sharing the remaining 63 per cent.

The reforms also provide more flexible payment arrangements and extend coverage to cancer care, kidney transplantation and cardiac surgery.

For other African countries, he said, the lesson is that health financing should involve governments, households and businesses rather than depend on a single source.

“Government, households, and the private sector each have a part to play, and a financing base built on that partnership is broader and more resilient than any one of them alone,” he said.

How Marburg Tested Rwanda’s Preparedness

Rwanda’s second lesson concerns the importance of investing in outbreak preparedness before emergencies occur.

Citing the 2024 Marburg outbreak, Nsengiyumva said Rwanda did not have to build an emergency response from scratch because it already had community health workers, surveillance networks, laboratories and hospitals serving the population.

These systems were mobilized within days to support the response. Community health workers screened more than 9.5 million people in a country of approximately 14 million, he said.

Rwanda brought the third-largest Marburg outbreak ever recorded under control within three months, with a case fatality rate of 22 per cent. Nsengiyumva described this as the lowest recorded rate for a disease that has historically killed up to nine in ten people infected.

He said the experience demonstrated why preparedness cannot depend on funding mobilized only after an outbreak begins. Countries need functioning health systems and trained personnel capable of responding quickly when threats emerge.

From Financing Commitments to Lives Saved

In his remarks, Sierra Leone President Julius Maada Bio argued that health sovereignty must be judged by whether governments can turn financial commitments into better services and fewer preventable deaths.

Bio reported that maternal deaths had declined by approximately 34 per cent and child deaths by 12 per cent compared with the corresponding period last year. The country had also reached 10,764 children who had never received routine vaccinations, exceeding its campaign target of 9,006.

He attributed the progress to a national campaign launched in March, with targets to reach zero preventable maternal deaths, zero preventable child deaths and zero children missing routine vaccination.

A central feature of the campaign is a weekly accountability system in which the Ministry of Health reviews maternal and child deaths with hospital and district teams every Friday. Officials examine what went wrong, identify delays and assign corrective actions to individuals with deadlines.

Sierra Leone has also trained health workers to manage obstetric emergencies, more than doubled referrals through its national emergency medical services and rebuilt and equipped blood banks in every regional hospital, Bio said.

Under a five-year national health compact requiring an estimated US$1.2 billion, Sierra Leone intends to finance 30 per cent through domestic resources and mobilize the remainder with development partners.

Africa CDC Director-General Dr Jean Kaseya echoed the call for greater African ownership, urging countries to strengthen their capacity to finance healthcare, manufacture medical products, lead outbreak responses and accelerate digital transformation.

Kaseya said the conference had attracted 46,217 registrations from 135 countries, making it the largest public health conference in the world.

African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf warned that African health systems remained too dependent on external resources, with recent reductions in international funding exposing their vulnerability.

“The health of our populations cannot continue to depend on the budgetary priorities of others,” Youssouf said.

MN202611_q3phxdiee7.t:
Tinubu made the disclosure at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family

Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu says the presidential villa suffers from cuts in electricity and water - failures that plague ordinary citizens.

He said he was shaving last week when the water supply at the villa, known as Aso Rock, in Abuja cut.

He is seeking re-election next January and vowed to address these issues..

Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family in Lagos.

He explained: "On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. In the villa, you won't know punishment dey dia too [there’s punishment there too in Nigerian pidgin].

"The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development. We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria,” he said.

Aso Villa serves as both the office and official residence of the Nigerian president. It is situated at the base of Aso Rock in Abuja.

Many Nigerians rely on generators like these to power their homes and businesses

Nigeria has long endured electricity shortages, but recent severe disruptions have been caused primarily by insufficient gas supplies and declining hydropower output, rather than the usual nationwide grid collapse.

Persistent blackouts in Lagos, Abuja and elsewhere have forced distribution companies to implement rotating power cuts, severely impacting households and businesses.

The country also suffers from chronic water shortages, the result of a structural crisis rooted in the gap between rapid urban population growth and decaying, inadequate public water infrastructure.

Tinubu made a high-profile electricity promise during the 2023 election campaign, but the exact wording and how binding it is has become a major point of contention ahead of the 16 January election.

Tinubu defeated the country’s former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as well as Peter Obi in 2023 and the three are seen as the strongest contenders once again.

Minisitiri w’Intebe w’u Rwanda, Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva, yasabye ibihugu bya Afurika gufata iya mbere mu gushaka ubushobozi bwo gutera inkunga inzego z’ubuzima, aho gukomeza kwishingikiriza ku nkunga zituruka mu mahanga zigenda zigabanuka, mu gihe ibibazo by’indwara n’ibindi bibazo by’ubuzima bikomeje kwiyongera.

Yabitangaje ku wa 23 Ugushyingo 2026, ubwo yitabiraga inama mpuzamahanga ya gatanu yiga ku buzima rusange muri Afurika (CPHIA 2026), yabereye i Addis Ababa muri Ethiopia.

Dr. Nsengiyumva yavuze ko kugabanuka kw’inkunga mpuzamahanga zigenerwa inzego z’ubuzima muri Afurika, mu gihe ibihugu bihanganye n’izamuka ry’indwara n’ibindi bibazo by’ubuzima, bikwiye kuba isomo rituma uyu mugabane wongera gutekereza ku buryo wifashisha umutungo wawo mu kwita ku baturage.

Yashimangiye ko Afurika idakwiye gukomeza kwishingikiriza ku bandi mu kubona ubushobozi bwo gutanga serivisi z’ibanze z’ubuzima.

Yagize ati: “Afurika igomba gufata inshingano zo gutera inkunga inzego zayo z’ubuzima.” Yongeyeho ko ibyo bidashatse kuvuga ko Afurika igomba guca ukubiri n’abafatanyabikorwa mpuzamahanga, ahubwo ko hakenewe ubufatanye bushya, aho ibihugu by’Afurika ari byo bigena ibyihutirwa n’ibigomba gukorwa, abafatanyabikorwa bakabishyigikira..

Mu ijambo rye, Minisitiri w’Intebe yavuze ko u Rwanda rudashaka kwerekana ko rufite ibisubizo by’ibibazo byose by’ubuzima, ariko ko ubunararibonye rwungutse mu kubaka urwego rw’ubuzima mu gihe cy’ubushobozi buke no guhangana n’ibyorezo bitandukanye, bushobora kubera andi mahanga isomo.

Isomo rya mbere yagarutseho ni ukwishakamo ubushobozi bwo gutera inkunga serivisi z’ubuzima.

Yagaragaje ko gahunda y'ubwisungane mu kwivuza, Mutuelle de Santé, imaze imyaka isaga 25 igira uruhare mu kongera umubare w’Abanyarwanda babasha kubona serivisi z’ubuvuzi.

Yavuze ko ubu ifasha hafi 89% by’Abanyarwanda kubona serivisi z’ubuzima, ndetse ikaba yarafashije mu kwagura uburyo abaturage babona imiti y'ibanze n'ubuvuzi bw’indwara zisaba ubuhanga bwihariye.

Yatanze n’indi mibare igaragaza intambwe u Rwanda rumaze gutera mu rwego rw’ubuzima kuva mu mwaka wa 2000. Yavuze ko impfu z’abana batarageza ku mwaka umwe zagabanutse ziva kuri 107 kuri buri bana 1.000 bavuka ari bazima, zigera kuri 27.

Impfu z’ababyeyi bapfa babyara na zo zagabanutse ziva kuri 1.071 kuri buri babyeyi 100.000 babyara, zigera kuri 149, mu gihe ikigereranyo cy’imyaka umuntu amara ku isi cyiyongereyeho imyaka igera kuri 20, kiva kuri 50 kigera kuri 70,5.

Yasobanuye ko ibyo byagezweho binyuze mu bikorwa bitandukanye birimo kongera abakozi b’ubuzima, gukoresha ikoranabuhanga no kubaka ibikorwa remezo by’ubuvuzi, ariko ko Mutuelle de Santé yagize uruhare rukomeye mu gufasha imiryango itari ifite ubushobozi bwo kwishyura kwivuza.

Yanagarutse ku ivugurura ry’uburyo ubwisungane mu kwivuza buterwa inkunga, avuga ko mu 2026 hashyizweho uburyo bwo gutanga umusanzu hashingiwe ku bushobozi bw’amikoro y’umuntu.

Muri ubwo buryo, abafite ubushobozi bwinshi batanga menshi, mu gihe abatishoboye kurusha abandi bishyurirwa na Leta.

Yavuze ko kuri ubu abanyamuryango batanga 37% by’amafaranga akoreshwa muri iyo gahunda, mu gihe 63% asigaye atangwa na Leta n’abikorera.

Yanavuze ko u Rwanda rwashyizeho uburyo bworoshye bwo kwishyura ubwisungane mu kwivuza ndetse rukagura serivisi zitangwamo, zirimo kuvura kanseri, guterwa impyiko no kubagwa umutima.

U Rwanda rwagaragaje ubunararibonye mu guhangana n'ibyorezo

Isomo rya kabiri Minisitiri w’Intebe yagarutseho ni ukutegura inzego z’ubuzima mbere y’uko ibyorezo byaduka, aho gutegereza ko ikibazo kiba ari bwo hatangwa amafaranga yo kugihashya.

Yatanze urugero rw’icyorezo cya Marburg cyagaragaye mu Rwanda mu 2024, avuga ko igihugu kitagombaga kongera kubaka inzego zo guhangana na cyo, kuko cyari gisanzwe gifite abajyanama b’ubuzima, inzego zigenzura indwara, laboratwari n’ibitaro byari bisanzwe bikorera abaturage.

Yavuze ko abajyanama b’ubuzima basuzumye abantu barenga miliyoni 9,5 mu gihugu cyari gifite abaturage hafi miliyoni 14.

Icyo cyorezo cyari mu byagaragaye ku rwego rw’isi bifite ubukana bukomeye, ariko u Rwanda rwabashije kugihashya mu gihe cy’amezi atatu gusa, umubare w’abacyanduye bapfuye ungana na 22%, ukaba ari wo muto wari wanditswe mu mateka y’iyo ndwara, kuko mu bihe byashize yagiye ihitana abagera kuri 90% by’abayanduye.

Yashimangiye ko ubushobozi bwo guhangana n’ibyorezo budakwiye kubakwa ari uko byadutse, ahubwo ko bugomba kuba igice gihoraho cy’inzego z’ubuzima.

Yanavuze ko kubera ko indwara z’ibyorezo zitubahiriza imipaka y’ibihugu, Afurika ikwiye gushyira imbaraga mu bufatanye bwambukiranya imipaka.

Yasabye Afurika kongera ubushobozi bwo gukora imiti n’inkingo

Isomo rya gatatu yagarutseho ni uko Afurika idashobora kuvuga ko yigenga mu rwego rw’ubuzima mu gihe ikomeje gutumiza mu mahanga imiti y’ingenzi, inkingo n’ibikoresho byifashishwa mu buvuzi.

Yavuze ko hakenewe gushyigikira inganda zo muri Afurika zikora imiti n’ibindi bikoresho by’ubuvuzi, binyuze mu kubaha amasoko ahamye no guhuza ubushobozi bw’ibihugu mu kugura ibikorerwa ku mugabane.

Yagaragaje ko uburyo bwo guhuriza hamwe amasoko y’ibihugu bya Afurika mu kugura ibikoresho n’imiti, buzafasha kongera umusaruro w’inganda zo kuri uyu mugabane.

Yanashimangiye ko ubufatanye mpuzamahanga bukwiye kujyana no guhererekanya ikoranabuhanga no kongera ubumenyi bw’abanyafurika.

Yavuze ko u Rwanda rwishimira kwakira Ikigo Nyafurika gishinzwe Imiti (African Medicines Agency) i Kigali, kandi ko rwiyemeje gushyigikira ko gitangira gukora neza no kuzuza inshingano zacyo.

Isomo rya kane ni ugushyira mu bikorwa ibyo ibihugu byiyemeje, bikabipimira ku musaruro ugaragara ku baturage.

Dr. Nsengiyumva yavuze ko Afurika idafite ikibazo cyo kubura amatangazo y’imigambi n’imbonerahamwe zigaragaza ibyo ibihugu byiyemeje, ahubwo ko icy’ingenzi ari ukureba niba amafaranga yageze ku bigo bitanga serivisi z’ubuzima kandi abarwayi bakabona impinduka.

Yasabye ko hakurikiranwa amafaranga atangajwe ko azatangwa n’ayo koko yatanzwe, ndetse igihe intego zitagezweho hakabaho isuzuma rigakurikirwa n’ingamba zo gukosora ibitagenda neza.

Mu gusoza, Minisitiri w’Intebe yashimangiye ko nta gihugu cya Afurika gishobora kwiyubakira cyonyine ubushobozi bwose gikenera mu rwego rw’ubuzima, bityo ko ibihugu bikwiye gufatanya mu gusangira ubumenyi, guhuriza hamwe amasoko no guteza imbere inganda zikorera ku mugabane.

Yagize ati: “Ubwigenge bwa Afurika mu rwego rw’ubuzima buzashingira cyane ku byo tuzubakira hamwe, nk’uko buzashingira ku byo buri gihugu kizageraho cyonyine.”

Yasoje asaba ibihugu bya Afurika gukorera hamwe kugira ngo uyu mugabane ugere ku ntego yo kwigira mu rwego rw’ubuzima no kubasha kwita ku baturage bawo.

Many Nigerian rely on boats to travel beyond their villages (file photo)

Search and rescue operations are racing against time in Nigeria after a boat carrying mourners travelling to a funeral capsized on Friday.

Twenty-nine bodies have been recovered and 50 people rescued so far, a spokesperson for the National Emergency Management Agency (Nema) told the BBC.

The government has responded by ordering stricter enforcement of safety standards on the country's inland waterways.

Overcrowding, poor maintenance and failure to observe safety regulations have contributed to previous deadly accidents on Nigeria's rivers.

The boat was travelling from Ayama community when it developed mechanical problems, according to police spokesperson Musa Mohammed.

Passengers asked the boat operator to steer towards land, but he allegedly declined, leading to the accident.

Survivors have described the panic that followed as passengers struggled to swim and stay afloat while waiting for emergency rescue services.

"As I swam, people were dragging me to the bottom, and I bit one woman and saved myself," Charity Ebikaboaere told local media outlet Arise News.

"Our things, our money, phones, everything lost, but me and my siblings are alive," said another survivor, Tari Samuel.

Why do Nigeria's boat disaster keep happening?

Nema spokesman Manzo Ezekiel raised concerns about the use of untrained boat operators and passengers travelling without life jackets.

"Some of them believe they're from river areas and they know how to swim," he said, warning that familiarity with waterways should not replace basic safety precautions.

The accident happened in a region where waterways are a key means of transport, especially for communities with limited road access.

"Overloading, speeding, recklessness and traveling without life jackets must stop. No journey is worth a life," Bayelsa Commissioner for Information Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai said in a statement on Saturday.

Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has relayed his condolences to the victims' families.

In a statement posted on X, Tinubu said he had directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to work together to ensure a successful rescue and recovery operation.

He also ordered that his election rally on Saturday, in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives.

Boat accidents are a recurring problem in Nigeria, particularly in riverine communities where boats are a major means of transport.

In August, at least 50 people, mostly children, died after an overloaded boat capsized in the north-western Sokoto state. In January, at least 25 people died when a leaking boat capsized in Yobe state, in the north-east.

The UN estimates that Israeli forces dropped more than 200,000 tonnes of explosives on Gaza in almost two years (file photo)

Gaza has been turned into "a toxic wasteland", with more than 99% of the Palestinian territory showing indicators of environmental contamination from Israeli military attacks, a new report from the non-profit organisation Oxfam says , external .

Heavy metals, explosive residues, and asbestos from destroyed buildings, dioxins and biological contaminants in the air, soil and water supply are threats to Palestinians now and potentially for decades to come, it says.

Oxfam International's executive director, Amitabh Behar, accuses Israel of "environmental war crimes" as part of an "ongoing genocide in Gaza."

"The destruction and contamination of Gaza will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival," he says.

Israel's government has been asked for its response to the report.

It has rejected genocide accusations in an ongoing case at the International Court of Justice as baseless and distorted. Israel maintains that its military campaign in Gaza is an act of self-defence against Hamas in response to the group's deadly attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, and that it takes steps to mitigate civilian harm.

The report says 99% of Gaza shows indicators of potential environmental contamination

Oxfam and the UK-based Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS) used satellite imagery, remote sensing, spatial analysis and other open-source data to draw their conclusions in the most comprehensive report to date on the severe environmental impacts caused by three years of intense war in Gaza.

The report details how munitions used in Israel's intense bombardment, as well as the debris from destroyed buildings and infrastructure, all have an impact on the environment. In February, a UN special rapporteur stated that more than 200,000 tonnes of explosives were dropped on Gaza in almost two years - "the equivalent of the total energy of approximately 13 Hiroshima-type nuclear bombs".

Last year, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) estimated that Israel's military operations destroying homes and infrastructure had generated more than 61 million tonnes of debris across the territory, with about 15% potentially carrying a high risk of contamination from hazardous materials.

"There are going to be chronic health impacts that are long term because a lot of these contaminants are persistent in the environment," Oxfam report author Lama Abdul Samad told the BBC.

She says that now and in future Gazans are likely to suffer from increased respiratory diseases, cancers, organ damage and a rise in birth defects and stillbirths.

Only a small fraction of the more than 60 million tonnes of debris in Gaza has been cleared

With all six wastewater treatment plants out of operation in Gaza, untreated sewage currently makes its way into groundwater and the Mediterranean Sea. The health impact has recently been exacerbated by heavy winter storms causing rainwater to mix with wastewater and flow through streets and tent sites housing displaced people.

Testing types and levels of contamination is often not possible because Gazan laboratories have been destroyed and there are Israeli restrictions on the entry of specialist testing equipment and scientists. The BBC has approached the Israeli military for comment.

UNEP said security concerns also prevented its expert staff from previously travelling to Gaza.

The Oxfam report calls for a full, independent environmental assessment to be carried out in Gaza to identify contamination risks ahead of a clean-up. It says special attention must be given to the protection of workers involved.

Recent winter storms caused rainwater to mix with wastewater and flow through streets and tent camps

Already, Gazan doctors have been reporting increased acute respiratory infections caused by dust and pollution from destroyed buildings and displaced people burning plastic, rags and cardboard to keep warm and cook food. Gastrointestinal diseases are linked to unsafe water and poor sanitation.

A Palestinian dermatologist, Dr Alaa Abu Hajar, told the BBC he had seen a five-fold increase in chronic skin diseases since the start of the war, putting this down to environmental pollution and overcrowded, unhygienic living conditions in tents and displacement camps.

"There are rodents, rubbish and sewage that's spread through the streets," he says. "Unfortunately, the age group most affected is children."

Dr Alaa Abu Hajar has seen a five-fold increase in chronic skin diseases since the start of the war

Farmers and those working in fishing say that pollution of the soil and sea mean they are unable to produce food that is safe.

"Sewage and wastewater are discharged into the sea without treatment and this is a great disaster," complains fisherman Abu al-Abed Sultan. "There is also rubble from destroyed houses that's dumped into the sea. When we lower our nets, we catch rubble and garbage. This harms the marine environment; the fish are affected and so are the fishermen."

At least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the war in Gaza, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. The UN says that humanitarian conditions remain dire.

Israel has conditioned large-scale Gaza reconstruction on the full disarmament of Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups. In July, Hamas accepted a plan put forward by the US-led Board of Peace to give up its weapons in exchange for an Israeli troop withdrawal. However, the Israeli government said the proposal was insufficient.

MN202611_16jna7bf7lx.t:
Sadio Mane was named best player at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations

Everyone knows a football match should take 90 minutes, but the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations has been playing out for 10 months.

Now, finally, Morocco or Senegal will be crowned winners. However, that moment of glory will come in a courtroom, not on the pitch.

On Tuesday afternoon sport's highest legal authority, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), will render its judgement on Senegal's appeal against the decision to strip them of the title they thought they won in January against the hosts in Rabat.

The case was heard in early October, and the wait is almost over.

With 66,000 fans creating an electric atmosphere in the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium, Morocco were chasing their first Afcon title since 1976.

But the final descended into chaos deep into second-half stoppage time.

With the match goalless, Senegal thought Ismaila Sarr had scored a dramatic winner, only to discover that referee Jean Jacques Ndala had blown for a Morocco free-kick.

The controversy deepened in the 98th minute when, after a video assistant referee (VAR) review, Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty.

Tempers boiled over on the touchline and in the stands. Senegal coach Pape Thiaw led some of his players and staff down the tunnel, while supporters clashed with security as order briefly collapsed.

Play eventually resumed and, in the 124th minute, Morocco missed a golden chance to end their 50-year wait for continental glory when Brahim Diaz failed to convert a penalty, chipping it 'Panenka' style into the arms of goalkeeper Edouard Mendy.

Pape Gueye's extra-time strike then secured a 1-0 win for Senegal, who lifted the trophy for a second time.

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FMRF) quickly lodged a complaint with the Confederation of African Football (Caf), arguing that Senegal had breached competition regulations.

Article 82, contained within a chapter titled 'Withdrawals', states: "If, for any reason whatsoever, a team... refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee", they shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated from the current competition".

In March a Caf appeals board agreed, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory.

While there is precedent for Caf overturning results during Afcon and World Cup qualifying, some people, including one former senior Caf official, argued that only the referee has the authority to abandon a match if a walk-off occurs.

The FMRF said it was seeking the proper application of tournament regulations, but Senegal's federation (FSF) described the ruling as "unfair, unprecedented and unacceptable" and appealed to Cas.

Some Senegal supporters were initially convicted of hooliganism offences after clashes during the final but eventually returned home after receiving a royal pardon

Founded in 1984 and based in the Swiss city of Lausanne, Cas was set up as an independent legal body designed to settle disputes as global sport became more lucrative and, as a result, more litigious.

For governing bodies which recognise Cas' authority, it is deemed to be the supreme arbiter, meaning its ruling is final unless, in rare cases, Switzerland's highest court decides to set it aside based on a limited number of technicalities.

More than 900 cases are filed every year, from more than 50 different sports, covering issues such as employment contracts and transfers, doping, corruption, TV rights and, in this case, the organisation of sporting events.

The FSF's appeal was heard in private on 8 October by a panel of three arbitrators chosen by Cas for their expertise in sports law.

The panel was led by Frenchman Gerald Simon, founder of the Sports Law Laboratory at the University of Burgundy and a Cas member for 23 years.

Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based attorney and professor of ​law at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas completed the trio.

If the panel had failed to come to a consensus on the case, Cas president Simon will have made the final decision.

Although Caf's appeals board is independent, a reversal of its judgement would deliver another blow to the reputation of African football's governing body, which has been heavily criticised for the retrospective decision to hand Morocco the title.

Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in March that it will "adhere to" and "respect" whatever Cas decides, so, if things go in Senegal's favour, it could mean someone having to tinker with the Afcon rulebook.

The Senegal walk-off has, however, already brought about a change in football's rules.

"The referee may sanction with a red card any player who leaves the field of play in protest at ⁠a ​referee's decision," said Ifab, the game's lawmaking body, in April.

"This new rule will also apply ​to any team official who incites players to leave the field of play. A team that causes a match ​to be abandoned will, in principle, forfeit the match."

Thiaw lost his job following Senegal's last-32 World Cup exit this summer, while Walid Regragui, the man in the Morocco dugout in January, was dismissed in March.

Whatever the outcome of the case, animosity is likely to linger between the two federations.

The FMRF's senior hierarchy was furious with Senegal's behaviour, believing the pictures beamed around the world irrevocably tarnished the image of the first Afcon hosted by the kingdom since 1988 - a tournament into which a huge amount of time and money had been invested.

The FSF and the Senegalese government have leaned into a feeling prevalent across the continent that Morocco holds too much influence within African football.

Other incidents also irked Senegal, such as laser pens being directed into players' eyes and ball boys moving goalkeeper Mendy's towel, something which led to the barely believable sight of reserve keeper Yehvann Diouf being tackled to the ground by three ball boys when he tried to intervene.

With the next Afcon scheduled to take place in June and July next year, the chances of a high-profile rematch between Africa's best two teams is a tantalising thought.

While the chaos of this year's final may have given birth to a new rivalry for fans to revel in, there is unanimous agreement that such encounters should be settled on the pitch and not in a courtroom.

Scotland women play Sweden in Paisley next Tuesday, with the second leg in Stockholm on 5 December

Scotland intend to bring fancied Sweden's World Cup dream "crashing down - and do it in a truly Scottish way", according to women's head coach Melissa Andreatta.

Scotland face a two-legged World Cup qualifying play-off against powerhouses Sweden, who are managed by Andreatta's former boss Tony Gustavsson.

The Swedes, who have been semi-finalists at the two previous Women's World Cups and are ranked eighth in the world, will be strong favourites to reach the tournament in Brazil next summer.

Andreatta, who has eight wins, two losses and four draws from her 14 games in charge of Scotland, was Gustavsson's deputy when he was Australia head coach from 2020 to 2024.

While the two have a connection from those years, the Australian is very much in business mode with next week's first leg at St Mirren Park looming.

"A few weeks ago Tony reached out, sent me a few messages and I took my time to respond," she told BBC Scotland.

"It wasn't much about football, just connecting on a personal level - which is probably a good thing, because I can be quite competitive. I just want to focus on business and not the personal level.

"I'm sure, like he is, all we're focused on is how we're going to win."

Listen to the full interview with Melissa Andreatta

The Scots finished top of their qualifying group earlier this year after four wins from their six games before beating the Czech Republic 5-2 on aggregate in the play-off semi-final.

That set up the exacting play-off final against the Swedes, a team who narrowly missed out on a spot in the final at the previous two World Cups.

Scotland have made just one appearance at the tournament, in 2019, and Andreatta is excited by the prospect of getting one over her old boss for her new home.

"It's going to be a great occasion to face them at home first," she added.

"They are such a powerhouse nation that carries so much expectation to go to their next tournament. We want to bring that all crashing down and do that in a truly Scottish way. That's what we're going to focus on.

"I definitely won't be looking at their dug out, I'll be focused on us and what we need to do to get the result and go to another tournament.

"They are an exceptional team but we won't be swayed by a team's reputation or ranking.

"We firmly believe that anything is possible. Once that whistle goes, if you've done the work and you're prepared you're in the position to make anything happen. With this group of players and staff I know that's possible, we can take it to anyone on any given day.

"It is a massive challenge but we love those moments and that's why we're here. We've earned it."

Melissa Andreatta with daughter Mackenzie after Scotland beat the Czech Republic in their World Cup qualification semi-final

There are more than 10,000 miles between Brisbane - where Andreatta grew up - and Ayr in Scotland, where she now calls home.

While the climate may be vastly different, there's one thing they do have in common - the beach.

"I love the coastal life. In Australia it's a big part of your lifestyle, being outdoors. I think there's something about the sea, being near it. Relaxing, calming, balancing," she said.

It has been 18 months since Andreatta was announced as Pedro Martinez Losa's successor as manager of the Scotland women's team and now, with her family alongside her - including two-year-old daughter Mackenzie - she feels at home.

"We've definitely settled in," she added. "We have the spots that we go to, our routine, we love it here. It's been a great landing spot for us on such a big move."

But what does her daughter make of her mum's job?

"She's got no idea," says Andreatta. "She just think's mum's on TV. Whenever she sees me she gets excited. Having her at the games is super special, being able to hold her on the pitch. She's such a joy.

"You do these things to make people proud and I want to make her proud."

Andreatta has made a promising start as Scotland manager - but now faces a huge task

Scotland without captain Weir for World Cup play-off

New strategy launched to transform Scottish women's football over 10 years

Andreatta was sitting in the pubs of Scotland over the summer as the Tartan Army headed over to the United States in their droves to watch the men's team compete at a first World Cup in almost 30 years.

The women won't have to wait that long if they can book a spot on the plane to Brazil next summer.

Andreatta is hoping to see just as many kilts on the Copacabana beach as there were in the bars of Boston.

"There is a strong desire among the group, not only players but also the staff, there is this desire to make their nation proud and show Scotland that the women's national team belongs here and deserves as much of the limelight as the men's," she added.

"Together we can make our nation proud and what better way to do it? To have our men at the World Cup and then the following summer our women.

"Watching from afar, what the fans did over there and in Boston, why can't we do that in Rio? That's what I'm envisaging but there's a lot to do and achieve before we get there."

MN202611_nza4lh2203.t:
Edward Iordanescu's most recent job was with Legia Warsaw, who he left in October 2025

Watford are set to appoint Edward Iordanescu as their new manager.

BBC Three Counties Radio report the Romanian is due to become the Hornets' sixth manager inside 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United in his 18th game in charge.

The 48-year-old is understood to be arriving in the UK on Tuesday to sign his contract and plans to bring three members of staff with him and hopes to be in the dugout for Wednesday's Championship fixture at home to Blackburn Rovers (19:45 GMT).

Iordanescu guided Romania at Euro 2024 where they topped their group ahead of Belgium with all four sides ending level on four points from three games before a 3-0 defeat against the Netherlands in the Round of 16.

Iordanescu - whose father Anghel had three spells in charge of the Romanian national team, leading them in two World Cups and two European Championships - left his last role at Polish club Legia Warsaw in October 2025.

It was the 48-year-old's ninth club over a 15-year coaching career which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj among others in his homeland.

Dionisi, who departed with the Hornets in 21st, four points above the relegation zone, was only appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.

Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.

The 46-year-old Italian was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared footage on social media which he says shows strikes on Russian vessels off the coast of Libya on Sunday.

A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones and the attack also hit a second vessel, a cargo ship which was being used to transport weapons, Zelensky said.

Footage verified by the BBC shows a ship ablaze at Benghazi's port.

The local health ministry said it had received injured people from a commercial ship that was targeted off the coast. It is not clear whether this is the same vessel as the one Ukraine has claimed responsibility for.

MN202611_11vt0c2lwsw.t:
Extra forces have been deployed to guard the facility where 'Chapo Isidro' is in custody

Mexican soldiers have detained eight alleged members of a drug cartel whose leader was arrested on Friday, sparking a wave of violence in northern Sinaloa state.

The Mexican defence ministry said the soldiers were shot by the suspects on Sunday while on patrol in the town of Sinaloa de Leyva, trying to re-establish order in the wake of the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.

Meza Flores, also known as "Chapo Isidro", was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list and had managed to evade capture for years.

The ministry said the eight had also been involved in the retaliatory violence unleashed by Meza Flores's cartel in the hours after his arrest on Friday.

In a statement published on social media , external , the ministry of defence said that one of the detainees was under age.

It added that its special forces had seized six vehicles as part of their operation, two of which had been fitted with bullet-proof armour and gun turrets.

The US Department of Justice described Friday's arrest of Meza Flores as "a spectacular military operation" and congratulated Mexico's military and special forces on his capture.

It said that the US Homeland Security Task Force had supported the Mexican military and praised the "bilateral effort".

Watch: Suspected drug lord 'El Chapo Isidro' transferred to Mexico's capital

Mexico's defence ministry said its special forces had used stealth and surprise to reach the home of the wanted man.

They also established a security perimeter to prevent Meza Flores from escaping and cartel reinforcements from arriving.

Nevertheless, a bloody firefight ensued.

Along with Meza Flores, his second-in-command, known as "Serafín", and his financial operator, were also arrested and quickly transferred by air to Mexico City.

As news of their arrest spread, members of their cartel erected barricades on major roads and set cars and some shops alight.

There were also reports of shoot-outs between the security forces and cartel members.

The prosecutor's office in Sinaloa says 17 people, four of them members of the Mexican security forces, were killed as a result of the violence on Friday and early Saturday.

US Assistant Attorney General A Tysen Duva has described Meza Flores as "the most dangerous man in Mexico".

"For decades Meza Flores has promoted the terrorist objectives of the Sinaloa cartel," Duva said, accusing him of "flooding the United States with deadly substances".

The 44-year-old is believed to have started his criminal career with the Juárez cartel decades ago.

He later moved on to become the right-hand man of the leader of the Beltrán Leyva Organisation, a drug gang once allied to the Sinaloa cartel before the two groups split and became bitter enemies.

As early as 2013, the US Treasury identified Meza Flores as the leader of his own drug-trafficking organisation, named after him.

The US Treasury said at the time, that the Meza Flores drug trafficking organisation was responsible for "the distribution of large quantities of methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and cocaine to the United States".

It added that the turf war between the Meza Flores cartel and the Sinaloa cartel had "resulted in the quadrupling of drug-war killings" in between 2009 and 2013.

According to think tank Insight Crime , external , Meza Flores himself kept a low profile over the last decade while continuing to run his cartel out of Guasave, in Sinaloa state.

The head of the US Drug Enforcement Administration said that his capture was a "significant blow to a ruthless criminal organisation that has used extreme violence to traffic deadly drugs, including fentanyl, a designated weapon of mass destruction, into American communities".

His arrest, and the co-operation between US and Mexican officials which led to it, will be seen as a win for the government of Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Sheinbaum has stressed that she is keen to work with the US authorities to capture high-profile target as long as Mexican's sovereignty is respected.

Dr. JAMES GASANA AND Dr. NKIKO NSENGIMANA

I followed with great interest the presentation of your recent book on “Radio TV ISHAKWE,” in an interview you gave to journalist Sixbert MUSANGAMFURA on November 11, 2026.

Your stated intention is to dismantle the colonial-made Hutu-Tutsi-Twa myth, according to which Hutu, Tutsi, and Twa are races. At the same time, you want to dismantle the colonial-made Hamitic myth.

On both points, I agree with you: Hutu, Tutsi, and Twa are not races. The Hamitic myth is indeed a colonial construct, and it must be deconstructed.

I am writing to you as a historian by training and a writer, to express my appreciation for the well-intentioned effort to deconstruct myths of colonial origin that constitute major obstacles to human fraternity and national and African unity.

At the same time, I am writing to draw your attention to the fact that the deconstruction approach, as you present it, risks producing the opposite effect of what you claim to be seeking.

You are replacing one myth with another. You are replacing Hutu-Tutsi-Twa with Nilotic-Bantu, and you are asserting that Rwandans came from Kenya and that the Ikinyarwanda language originated from the Luo language.

However, you have not presented what historical linguistics requires for such a claim:

1. What are the regular cognates, with systematic phonetic rules, between Luo and Kinyarwanda?

2. How do you explain that Kinyarwanda is defined by renowned linguists, such as André Coupez, as a 100% Bantu language in its grammar, basic vocabulary, and morphology?

3. How can you conclude, based on words gleaned here and there, that the name of our beloved homeland, Urwanda—whose meaning you also caricature by calling it IKINTU CYANDA—comes from the Luo word “anda,” which belongs to the Nilotic language family?

4. In formal logic, when the premises are false, the conclusion is also false. Do you know that this is the case for your thesis, whose purely negationist neo-colonial extrapolations drag the URWANDA Nation and the Rwandan People from Kenya?

5. Supposing, in the impossible, that your linguistic approach is true, why wouldn’t the opposite be true?

6. Do your respective PhD degrees give you the necessary and sufficient intellectual tools and authority to engage in a field so tricky for amateurs in comparative linguistics and geohistory of any level?

7. Why replace one 19th-century colonial category with another colonial category from the same century, instead of working on Rwandan social reality with a more pro-independence, fraternal, and unitarist approach than a divisive one?

But beyond the method, there is a more serious issue at stake.

By claiming that the Tutsi do not exist as a group, you open the door to a dangerous line of reasoning, not far removed from Holocaust denial: there are no Tutsis, therefore the genocide against the Tutsi is a political fabrication. Even if this is not your intention, it is, in any case, the logical consequence of your thesis, if left unspecified.

However, History and Law are clear: a group does not need to be a race to be the victim of a genocide. It is enough that it be designated as such by the killers and experienced as such by the victims. In 1994, Tutsis were killed because they were identified as Tutsis: identity cards, roadblocks, lists, the National radio station, RTLM, the importation of machetes to slit throats, the funding and training of militias for this purpose, hate speech at official rallies, the most memorable of which was delivered by the infamous Léon Mugesera in Kabaya on November 22, 1992; etc., etc.

Dismantling a colonial myth should not be used to erase the memory of the Genocide against the Tutsis. We can be one Rwandan people and simultaneously recognize that it was as Tutsis that more than a million people were targeted in 1994. These two truths are compatible, and they must remain so.

Pending the opportunity to conduct a more comprehensive review based on your bibliography, I therefore ask you, publicly and fraternally, to answer these seven questions with evidence and to clarify your position on 1994. Scholarly debate deserves better than mere semantic similarities. The memory of the victims deserves better than shifting the debate toward the external origins of a People and a Nation.

Awaiting your response, I remain, dear Gentlemen, yours sincerely.

Amb. Isaïe MURASHI is former diplomat and Parliarmentarian. He is a historian and commentator on national and regional issues. He has authored two books. He is also the Resident Historian for ‘Urubuga rw’Amateka’ , a podcast published weekly on Kigali Today YouTube channel , run by Kigali Today Ltd

Next said it was informed by one of its suppliers about the incident

Next has said that some of its data has been accessed in a cyber breach affecting a third-party online supplier.

The high street retailer said there was no evidence that customers' personal data had been compromised.

The firm - which has its headquarters in Enderby, Leicestershire - said it had been informed by one of its suppliers about the incident, which led to "unauthorised access to certain benign data relating to Next".

"We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier," the company told investors.

"Our investigations are ongoing. However, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised.

"The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or Next."

The company added it was treating the situation "with the utmost seriousness", and working with the supplier as well as the police and regulators.

Next is the latest retailer to be caught up in a cyber breach.

In October, Asos said an "unauthorised party" had gained access to an employee's account , leading customers to receive a phone alert saying that the retailer had been hacked.

The firm said the attacker gained access to some personal data, including names and contact details belonging to customers.

In 2025 Marks & Spencer suffered from a major cyber-attack, which forced it to stop all online sales for about six weeks and led to some empty shelves in shops.

During the trial, the prosecution described Kurtaj as a "leading light" in the teen gang Lapsus$

A cyber criminal who hacked the maker of Grand Theft Auto has been released on licence after serving the majority of a seven-year sentence.

Multiple offender Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, was released from custody with the judge warning him: "Don't let this happen again."

The now 21-year-old hacked several companies and individuals, including GTA 6-maker Rockstar Games, whom he tried to extort after stealing clips of the unfinished game in 2022.

Kurtaj had pleaded guilty last Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

Kurtaj was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.

But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.

Now, he has been sentenced and released on the same day.

He has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order which will last five years. It restricts his activity online including barring him from using Telegram and Discord.

City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

He hacked Rockstar games, Revolut and Uber while on bail and under police protection in a Travelodge in Bicester.

He was there for protection from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6, which had been shrouded in secrecy until its release last week.

He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."

GTA 6 was released to much fanfare last week

The company refused to co-operate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.8m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

When he was sentenced he stood and smiled.

He had short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie.

The hacker blinked frequently during the hearing.

The Judge Mr Justice Turner told him "you are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again."

Kurtaj's defence team said he found the online world a more comfortable way of interacting with other people.

"The restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour and interests that are a core feature of ASD [autism spectrum disorder] led him to become preoccupied with the online world where he felt better able to function and exist," they said.

They said he was exposed to people who showed him how to cheat at games and then to "people who were involved in hacking".

During the pandemic, he was "very isolated" and his "connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously," they added.

Kurtaj's Snapchat posts were the first sign for reporters that he had been released from a secure hospital

Kurtaj and the gang's other hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber used social engineering techniques - tricking people into clicking malicious links or giving up sensitive information - to gain access to internal systems.

Previously, the court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.

Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 (£230,000) from individual victims.

Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents.

In prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga n’Ubutwererane, Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, yasuye uruganda rwa CopenHill ruherereye mu Mujyi wa Copenhagen muri Danemark, asobanurirwa uburyo ikoranabuhanga rishobora gufasha guhindura imyanda isoko y’ingufu, mu gihe rinagira uruhare mu kurengera ibidukikije no guteza imbere imijyi.

Uru ruzinduko rwagaragaje uburyo Danemark iri mu bihugu byateye imbere mu bukungu bwisubira (Circular Economy), aho ibikoresho byari kuba imyanda byongera gukoreshwa cyangwa bigahindurwamo ibindi bifite akamaro mu buzima bwa buri munsi.

CopenHill ni urugero rwihariye rw'uburyo ibibazo by’imicungire y’imyanda bishobora guhindurwamo amahirwe y’iterambere, binyuze mu guhuza ikoranabuhanga, kurengera ibidukikije no kubyaza umusaruro umutungo usanzwe ufatwa nk’udafite akamaro.

Gukusanya imyanda no kuyibyazamo ingufu ni imwe mu nzira zishobora gufasha ibihugu kugabanya umubare w’imyanda ijugunywa ahantu hatandukanye, no kongera amasoko y’ingufu zikoreshwa mu ngo no mu bikorwa by’inganda.

U Rwanda rushobora kungukira byinshi muri ubu buryo, cyane ko imijyi yarwo ikomeje kwaguka, umubare w’abaturage ukiyongera ndetse n’imyanda ikomoka mu ngo, amasoko, amahoteli n’inganda ikomeza kwiyongera.

Gukoresha ikoranabuhanga rihindura imyanda ingufu byafasha u Rwanda kugabanya imyanda ijyanwa mu bimoteri, kongera ingufu z'amashanyarazi n'ubushyuhe, ndetse no kugabanya ingaruka ziterwa n’imyanda ku buzima bw’abaturage no ku bidukikije.

Byanagira uruhare mu guteza imbere ubukungu bwisubira, aho imyanda idafatwa nk’ikintu cyo kujugunya gusa, ahubwo ikitabwaho nk'umutungo ushobora kongera kubyazwa umusaruro.

U Rwanda rwamaze gushyiraho ingamba zo guteza imbere ubukungu burengera ibidukikije no guhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ikirere. Binyuze muri gahunda y’igihugu y’ubukungu bwisubira (National Circular Economy Action Plan), yatangijwe mu 2022, rwiyemeje guteza imbere uburyo bwo gukoresha neza umutungo no kugabanya imyanda.

Ikindi kandi, amabwiriza y’u Rwanda ajyanye no gucunga imyanda yo mu mijyi agaragaza ko hakwiye kwigwa uburyo imyanda idashobora kongera gukoreshwa yahindurwamo ingufu, harimo n’uburyo bwo kuyibyazamo biogaz.

Gusa kugira ngo ubu buryo bushobore gushyirwa mu bikorwa mu Rwanda, byasaba ubushakashatsi ku bwinshi n'ubwoko bw'imyanda iboneka, ikiguzi cy'ibikorwa remezo, ubushobozi bw'ikoranabuhanga, n'uburyo bwo kugenzura imyuka ishobora kwangiza ikirere.

Ni ngombwa kandi kubanza gutandukanya imyanda ishobora kongera gukoreshwa n'itagishobora gukoreshwa, kugira ngo gutwika imyanda bitabangamira gahunda yo kuyitunganya no kuyisubiramo.

CopenHill ni urugero rwerekana ko guhangana n’ikibazo cy’imyanda bishobora no kuba inzira yo kubona ingufu, guteza imbere ubukungu no kubaka imijyi irambye.

US rapper Don Toliver has postponed his concert at the O2 arena in London on Monday, a day after his show in Manchester was evacuated following an "unknown substance" being released into the crowd.

"I'm very sad to sit here and say I have to reschedule The O2 London show to December 15th due to unfortunate incident last night Manchester," he wrote on Instagram.

"I just wanna make sure everyone is safe and the next show goes on properly. My heart and prayers are with with everyone that was injured last night."

One person was taken to hospital and more than 80 were assessed for "eye and respiratory symptoms" after the incident during Toliver's show at the Co-op Live arena on Sunday night.

Watch: Coughs, confusion and boos as Co-op Live concert cancelled

Fans described "distressing scenes" with people "choking", "screaming" and "coughing up blood" because of the effects of an unknown substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) declared a major incident and are investigating.

The force said 12,000 people had been evacuated after the incident at around 22:00 GMT.

Postponing the O2 arena show, promoter Live Nation blamed "production delays following last night's show at Co-op Live in Manchester".

A statement added: "We are sorry to everyone affected by last night's events in Manchester and full refunds for that show will be automatically processed to ticket holders."

Police investigate unknown substance that caused Manchester's Co-op Live evacuation

'People were screaming in pain' during Co-op Live evacuation

Some fans complained about security and a lack of searches going in to the Manchester concert.

Co-op Live said on its website there were a range of security measures, and while "some of these are visible, others you won't be able to see".

There have been apparently similar incidents earlier on his tour, when some fans reported that spray or gas were released in the crowd in Zurich and Paris.

"The only thing I love more than creating music is performing for my fans," Toliver said in his statement, asking people to stop bringing substances into his shows.

"It ain't cool," added the rapper, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards earlier this month. "See you soon London, love you Guys. DT."

Toliver's Nitrous tour, named after his new album, is also due to visit Wembley Arena in London on Tuesday. No update has been given about that show.

Minisitiri w’Ibidukikije, Arakwiye Bernadette, kuri uyu wa mbere tariki 23 Ugushyingo 2026 yagejeje ku Nteko Rusange y’Umutwe w’Abadepite Umushinga w’itegeko rishyiraho Ikigega cy’Ibidukikije n’Ihinduka ry’Ibihe mu Rwanda agaragaza ko FONERWA imaze gukusanya miliyoni 364 z’amadolari mu bikorwa byo kurengera ibidukikije.

Mu mishinga y’ingenzi yatewe inkunga n’iki kigega harimo Green Gicumbi, wahawe miliyoni 32 z’amadolari ya Amerika. Uyu mushinga wagiriye akamaro abantu bagera ku 150.000 mu buryo butaziguye, ni ukuvuga abahawe ubufasha cyangwa serivisi zawo ubwabo, mu gihe abandi 380.000 bawungukiyemo mu buryo buziguye, babikesha impinduka nziza wazanye mu mibereho y’abaturage no mu kubungabunga ibidukikije.

Ati “Uyu mushinga warimo ibikorwa byo gucunga neza imigezi n’ibibaya by’amazi, guteza imbere ubuhinzi bwita ku mihindagurikire y’ikirere, no guteka hifashishijwe ibicanwa cyangwa ikoranabuhanga bitangiza cyane ubuzima bw’abantu n’ibidukikije, ugereranyije n’inkwi n’amakara. no kwimura abantu batuye mu bice bishobora guteza ibyago”.

Ministiri yavuze ko uyu mushinga wanagize uruhare mu guhanga imirimo n’amahirwe yo guteza imbere ubumenyi birenga 23.000 mu Karere ka Gicumbi.

Hari kandi umushinga wa Nyandungu Eco-Park watwaye miliyoni eshanu z’amadolari ya Amerika. Wagizemo uruhare mu gusana no kubungabunga urusobe rw’ibinyabuzima, gucunga imyuzure no gutegura gahunda yo gusana ibishanga bifite ubuso bugera kuri hegitari 4.000 muri Kigali.

Undi mushinga ni uwa Ampersand, watewe inkunga ingana na miliyoni 600 z’amafaranga y’u Rwanda. Wafashije mu igeragezwa ry’ikoreshwa ry’ibinyabiziga bikoresha amashanyarazi no gukurura ishoramari ry’abikorera riri hagati ya miliyoni 30 na 40 z’amadolari ya Amerika.

FONERWA igiye kuva ku gutanga inkunga gusa ijye no gushora imari

Umushinga w’itegeko rishyiraho Ikigega cy’Ibidukikije n’Ihinduka ry’Ibihe mu Rwanda uteganya guhindura imikorere ya FONERWA, ikava ku kuba ikigega ahanini gitanga inkunga kikagira n’ubushobozi bwo gukusanya no gushora imari mu mishinga irengera ibidukikije no guhangana n’ihinduka ry’ibihe.

Ibi biri mu mpinduka z’ingenzi ziteganywa n’umushinga w’itegeko Minisitiri w’Ibidukikije, Arakwiye Bernadette, yagejeje ku Nteko Rusange y’Umutwe w’Abadepite.

FONERWA yashyizweho n’Itegeko No 39/2017, ikora ishingiye ahanini ku nkunga z’abafatanyabikorwa mu iterambere no gutera inkunga imishinga.

Imbogamizi zagaragajwe na Minisitiri Dr Arakwiye zirimo kugabanuka kw’inkunga n’inguzanyo zitangwa ku buryo bworoshye, ubushobozi buke bwo gukusanya imari nini ituruka ku bashoramari bigenga n’ibigo by’imari, ndetse no kutagira uburyo buhagije bwo kwinjiza amafaranga no kongera kuyashora mu yindi mishinga.

Ati “Ni muri urwo rwego umushinga w’itegeko uteganya ko iki kigega kizajya gikusanya imari, kiyihuza, kiyishora mu mishinga itandukanye kandi kikongera gukoresha amafaranga cyinjije”.

Izi mpinduka zigamije gutuma ikigega kibasha gukomeza ibikorwa byacyo mu buryo burambye, kidashingiye gusa ku nkunga z’abafatanyabikorwa, ahubwo kinifashisha ishoramari ry’abikorera n’andi masoko y’imari.

MN202611_18sszrrfdrp.t:
Ibi bigaragazwa na gahunda y’igihugu y’ibikorwa bigamije kugabanya imyuka ihumanya ikirere no guhangana n’ingaruka z’ihinduka ry’ibihe, izwi nka NDC 3.0, nk’uko byatangajwe na Minisitiri w’Ibidukikije Dr Bernadette Arakwiye kuri uyu wa mbere tariki 23 Ugushyingo 2026 ageza umushinga w’itegeko rishyiraho Ikigega cy’Ibidukikije n’Ihinduka ry’Ibihe mu Rwanda ku Nteko Ishinga Amategeko Umutwe w’Abadepite.

Minisitiri Dr Bernadette Arakwiye yabwiye Abadepite ko amafaranga akenewe ari menshi, bityo hakaba hakenewe ubundi buryo bwo gukusanya imari, burimo n’ishoramari ry’abikorera ndetse n’imari ihuriweho n’inzego za Leta n’abikorera.

Ati “Ku rundi ruhande, inkunga n’inguzanyo bitangwa ku buryo bworoshye bigenda bigabanuka, aho inyandiko igaragaza ko byagabanutse ku rugero rwa 10% kugeza kuri 20% mu myaka ya vuba”.

Kubera igabanuka ry’inkuru aha niho Minisitiri yavuze ko ikigega cy’Ibidukikije kigiye kugira ishami ryihariye ry’ishoramari.

Ati “ Umushinga w’itegeko rishyiraho Ikigega cy’Ibidukikije n’Ihinduka ry’Ibihe mu Rwanda uteganya gushyiraho ishami ryihariye ry’ishoramari rizajya rihuza imari ituruka ku bashoramari b’ibigo n’abikorera, rikayishora mu mishinga itandukanye irambye”.

Iri shami rizaba rifite ubuzima gatozi kandi rikora nk’ikigo cyigenga, rikazajya rikoresha uburyo n’inyandiko by’ishoramari mu guhuza imari y’imigabane ituruka ku bashoramari no kuyishyira mu mishinga ishobora kubyara inyungu.

Uretse iri shami, umushinga uteganya ko ikigega kizajya gitanga ubujyanama bwa tekiniki ku bategura imishinga, abashoramari n’abandi bafatanyabikorwa. Ibyo bizabafasha gutegura imishinga inoze no kuyishyira mu bikorwa.

Ati “Ni muri urwo rwego u Rwanda rushyize imbere uburyo bwo gukusanya no guhuza imari ituruka ahantu hatandukanye, kugira ngo ibikorwa byo kurengera ibidukikije no guhangana n’ihinduka ry’ibihe bibone ubushobozi bukenewe”.

Mu Rwanda, raporo y’igihugu ku ntego zo guhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ibihe igaragaza ko kugeza mu 2024, rwari rumaze gukusanya hafi miliyari 4,8 z’amadolari ya Amerika avuye mu nzego za Leta n’abikorera, abafatanyabikorwa mpuzamahanga n’ubundi buryo bwo kubona imari.

Icyakora, haracyari icyuho cya miliyari 6,2 z’amadolari y’America kugira ngo intego zari ziteganyijwe kugeza mu 2030 zigerweho. Byongeye kandi, u Rwanda rukeneye hafi miliyari 12 z’amadolari mu gihe cya 2025–2035 kugira ngo rushyire mu bikorwa ingamba zo kugabanya imyuka ihumanya ikirere no guhangana n’ingaruka z’imihindagurikire y’ibihe. Ibi bituma rukomeza gushaka imari no kongera uruhare rw’abikorera mu ishoramari ry’ibidukikije ari bimwe mu byarufasha kugera ku ntego rwiyemeje.

Akanama nkemuramapaka ka Siporo ku isi, kuri uyu wa mbere taliki ya 23 Ugushyingo kamenyesheje impuzamashyirahamwe y’umupira w’amaguru muri Afurika (CAF), ishyirahamwe ry’umupira w’amaguru muri Maroke na Senegal ko kuri uyu wa kabiri taliki ya 24 ugushyingo aribwo kaza kubashykiriza umwanzuro wavuye mu bujurire bwa Senegal bwo kwamburwa igikombe n’akanama k'Ubujurire ka CAF kigahabwa Maroke nyamara yari yatsindiwe ku mukino wa nyuma.

Taliki ya 18 Mutarama 2026, nibwo hakinwe umukino wa nyuma w’igikombe cy’Afurika cya cya 2025, i Rabat ho muri Maroke ari nayo yari yakiriye iki gikombe. Ubwo umukino wari urimbanyije, imvururu zatangiye ku munota wa 90+2 w’iminota y’inyongera kuko iminota 90 yari yarangiye ari 0-0.

Umukinnyi w’ikipe ya Senegal Ismaïla Sarr yatsindiye Sénégal igitego n'umutwe, ariko umusifuzi Jean-Jacques Ndala acyanga avuga ko myugariro wa Sénégal, Abdoulaye Seck, yari yakoreye ikosa Achraf Hakimi mbere y'uko igitego kijyamo. Nyuma y'iminota mike gusa, rutahizamu wa Maroke, Brahim Díaz, yaguye mu rubuga rw'amahina nyuma yo gukorwaho ikosa na El Hadji Malick Diouf. Umusifuzi nyuma yo kwitabaza ikoranabuhanga rya VAR maze yemeza ko ari penaliti ya Maroc.

Kubera uburakari bw'igitego cyabo cyari cyanzwe n'iyo penaliti babonaga ko itari ikwiye, umutoza wa Sénégal, Pape Thiaw, yahise asaba abakinnyi be kuva mu kibuga. Bamwe mu bakinnyi basubiye mu rwambariro, umukino uhagarara iminota igera kuri 14.

ku munota 90+23’, Nyuma yo kwingingwa cyane na kapiteni wabo Sadio Mané wasanze bagenzi be mu rwambariro akabasaba kugaruka kurangiza umukino, abakinnyi ba Sénégal baragarutse maze Brahim Díaz atera ya penaliti (mu buryo bwa Panenka)ku bw’amahirwe macye ya Maroke ifatwa neza n'umunyezamu Édouard Mendy.

umukino waramoje maze Pape Gueye ku mupira wari uvuye kuri Idrissa Gana Gueye, atera ishoti rikomeye cyane n'akaguru k'ibumoso rigana mu nguni yo hejuru y'izamu rya Yassine Bounou maze Senegal itsinda igitego cya mbere ari nacyo cyasoje umukino maze Senegal yegukana Igikombe ityo.

Ntabwo byarangiriye aho kuko taliki ya 17 Werurwe 2026 nyuma y’ubujurire bwa Maroke (FRMF) ,Akanama k'Ubujurire ka CAF kemeje ko Sénégal yatewe mpaga kubera kuva mu kibuga nta ruhushya rw'umusifuzi, byatumye ihabwa igihano cyo gutsindwa ibitego 3-0 maze maroke igahabwa igikombe cy’ Afuria cya 2025.

Taliki ya wa 25 Werurwe 2026, Ishyirahamwe ry'Umupira w'Amaguru muri Sénégal (FSF) ryatanze ikirego muri TAS risaba ko icyemezo cya CAF gitesha agaciro Sénégali ikagumana igikombe cyayo yegukanye itsinze Maroke. Senegare yatanze ikirego ishingiye ku ngingo ivuga ko amategeko y'umupira w'amaguru ateganya ko icyemezo cy'umusifuzi mu kibuga ari ntakuka, kandi ko umusifuzi Jean-Jacques Ndala yemeye ko umukino ukomeza kugeza urangiye.

Taliki ya 8 Ukwakira 2026, TAS yaburanishije urubanza rwaburanishijwe mu muhezo i Lausanne mu Busuwisi rukaba rwaramaze amasaha arenga atanu ruhuza abahagarariye Sénégal, Maroc ndetse na CAF.

Amategeko agenga imikino ya CAN niya FIFA ni yo yari ku isonga mu byaranze uru rubanza rwa Sénégal, Maroc, na CAF muri TAS. Impande zombi zashingiraga cyane ku ngingo zivuguruzanya hagati y’ububasha bw’umusifuzi mu kibuga n’ibihano biteganywa iyo ikipe ivuye mu kibuga.

1. Ingingo Sénégal yishingikirizagaho (Ububasha bw'umusifuzi)

. Itegeko rya 5 rya FIFA (Laws of the Game - Law 5). Iri tegeko rivuga ko ibyemezo by'umusifuzi mu kibuga ku bijyanye n'imigendekere y'umukino ari ntakuka kandi ko umukino uba warangiye iyo umusifuzi awushoje ku mugaragaro. Sénégal ivuga ko umusifuzi Jean-Jacques Ndala atasoje umukino ngo atange mpaga, ahubwo yakomeje umukino kugeza urangiye.

. Ihame ryo kutaburanisha ibyabaye mu kibuga (Field of Play Doctrine). Urukiko rwa TAS rusanzwe rufite ihame ryo kutivanga mu byemezo by'abasifuzi byafatiwe mu kibuga mu gihe umukino ukomeje, keretse iyo hari ibimenyetso bya ruswa cyangwa uburiganya.

2. Ingingo Maroc na CAF bishingikirizaho (Guta ikibuga / Abandonment)

. Ingingo ya 82 n'iya 84 z'amategeko agenga CAN (AFCON Regulations). Aya mategeko asobanura neza ko ikipe yose ivuye mu kibuga idahawe uburenganzira n'umusifuzi, cyangwa ikanga gukomeza umukino, ifatwa nk'iyikuye mu irushanwa maze igaterwa mpaga (forfeit) y'ibitego 3-0.

. Iyi imyitwarire ya CAF (CAF Disciplinary Code - Ingingo ya 148). Maroc ivuga ko kuba abakinnyi ba Sénégal baramaze iminota 14 hanze y'ikibuga byahungabanyije umukino mu buryo butemewe n'amategeko, bityo Akanama k'Ubujurire ka CAF kari gafite ububasha bwo gufata icyemezo nyuma y'umukino gashingiye kuri raporo y'umusifuzi n'iya komiseri w'umukino.

Ndayishimiye yabivugiye mu muhango wo gusoza icyumweru cyahariwe abarwanyi b’ishyaka CNDD-FDD, wabereye kuri Stade Ingoma i Gitega ku wa 21 Ugushyingo 2026.

Yavuze ko Kagame, wari Visi Perezida w’u Rwanda akaba na Minisitiri w’Ingabo icyo gihe, yaba yarahuriye n’abanyeshuri b’Abatutsi kuri Campus Kiriri i Bujumbura, akabashishikariza kwica bagenzi babo b’Abahutu.

Perezida w’u Burundi kandi yavuze amagambo avuga ko Kagame yaba yarabwiye abo banyeshuri ko adasobanukiwe uburyo abanyeshuri b’Abatutsi bashobora kwicarana n’Abahutu, ashingiye ku kuba Abahutu baragize uruhare muri Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi mu Rwanda.

Ibi birego byahise bikurura impaka, kuko mu nkuru y;Ikinyamakuru SOS Médias Burundi hagaragara ko “Ndayishimiye atatanze inyandiko, ubuhamya bwigenga cyangwa ibindi bimenyetso byashobora kwifashishwa mu kwemeza ko iyo nama yabaye ndetse n’amagambo avuga ko Kagame yayivugiyemo.”

Ubwicanyi bw’abanyeshuru b’abahutu Ndayishimiye avuga ko bwabereye muri Kaminuza y’u Burundi mu ijoro ryo ku wa 11 Kamena 1995, SOS Médias yo ivuga ko bwabereye ku ma Campus ya Mutanga, Kamenge na Kiriri i Bujumbura, ndetse no kuri Campus ya Zege i Gitega.

Ku mbuga nkoranyambaga, hari abagaragaje ko ibirego nk’ibi bikomeye bisaba ibimenyetso bishobora kugenzurwa.

Uwitwa Pollownox kuri X yavuze ko ikibazo cy’u Rwanda cyakunze gukoreshwa nk’igikoresho cyo gusobanura ibibazo bya politiki n’umutekano byo mu karere.

Mu magambo ye, yagize ati “Nine crises, one answer, zero accountability”, bishatse kuvuga ngo “intambara icyenda, igisubizo kimwe, nta buryozwe na mbe,” ashimangira ko buri kibazo gishobora kurangira hashinjwe u Rwanda aho gusobanura uruhare rw’abayobozi mu gukemura ibibazo byabo.

N’uwitwa Florentine Kabasinga yagaragaje impungenge ku buremere bw’ibyo birego, avuga ko gushinja Perezida w’u Rwanda kuba yarategetse cyangwa yashishikarije abanyeshuri b’Abatutsi kwica Abahutu mu 1996, cyangwa mu gihe cyavuzwe na Ndayishimiye, ari ikirego gikomeye cyane kandi gisaba ibimenyetso bifatika.

Kabasinga yavuze ko nta bimenyetso byagaragajwe bishimangira ibyo birego, anenga uburyo amakuru nk’ayo ashobora gukwirakwizwa n’imbuga abona ko zifite imvugo zirwanya u Rwanda.

Yibajije kandi niba koko byumvikana ko umuyobozi wari ufite ububasha bwo gushishikariza kwihorera nyuma ya Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi mu Rwanda, ariko agahitamo gushyigikira inzira yo kubana no kwiyunga, ari we waba waragiye i Bujumbura gushishikariza abantu kwihorera ku Banyeshuri b’Abahutu.

Nubwo SOS Médias ivuga ko Ndayishimiye yashingiye ku byabaye mu gihe yari umunyeshuri w’Umuhutu waje kwinjira mu mutwe wa FDD, inkuru kandi igaragaza ko amateka y’ubwicanyi bwo mu Burundi akomeje kuba isoko y’ubusobanuro butandukanye.

Komisiyo y’Ukuri n’Ubwiyunge y’u Burundi yakoze ubushakashatsi ku bahitanywe n’ubwicanyi bwo mu 1995, aho mu 2020 yari imaze gutangaza ko abanyeshuri 109 bishwe bari bamaze kumenyekana.

Ibi birego kandi bije mu gihe umubano w’u Rwanda n’u Burundi ukomeje kuba mubi, aho ibihugu byombi bimaze igihe bishinjanya ibibazo by’umutekano, cyane cyane ku bibera mu Burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo.

SOS Médias ivuga ko umubano w’ibihugu byombi wakomeje kuzamo amakimbirane, u Burundi bushinja u Rwanda gushyigikira umutwe wa RED-Tabara, mu gihe u Rwanda ruhakana ibyo birego. Ku kibazo cya RDC, u Burundi na RDC bishinja u Rwanda gushyigikira M23, mu gihe u Rwanda na rwo rushinja u Burundi na RDC gukorana na FDLR.

Bityo, amagambo mashya ya Ndayishimiye yongeye gushyira amateka y’ubwicanyi bwo mu karere hagati mu mpaka za politiki, ariko kugeza ubu, nk’uko SOS Médias ibitangaza, nta bimenyetso byigenga byashyizwe ahagaragara bihamya ko Perezida Kagame yaba yarateguye cyangwa yashishikarije ubwo bwicanyi bw’abanyeshuri b’Abahutu.

David Raya is Arsenal's first choice goalkeeper and has won the Golden Glove for the last three seasons in the Premier League.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya's shoulder injury "doesn't look too serious", but he will miss Tuesday's Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta.

Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.

He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula.

"We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging," said Gunners boss Arteta.

"He is not fit [to face Dortmund] but it doesn't look too serious."

Arteta said that while the incident looked pretty innocuous the pain his keeper was in made him fear it was a serious injury.

"With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected," said Arteta.

"When you look at the action it doesn't seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment.

"The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let's see."

Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him?

Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City , Brentford , Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in their next tranche of matches.

And Raya is huge part of the way that Arsenal play because of his ability with the ball at his feet.

When asked if losing Raya for a long period of time would be the biggest blow to his team, Arteta said: "We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa [Arrizabalaga] and Illan [Meslier].

"Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan."

Ibi byagarutsweho mu nama ya 2026 Korea-Rwanda Seminar on Cooperation in AI Education, yahuje inzego z’uburezi zo mu Rwanda na Koreya y’Epfo, yabereye muri Kigali Serena Hotel kuri uyu wa Mbere, tariki ya 23 Ugushyingo 2026, ifite insanganyamatsiko igira iti: “Preparing Future Talent in the AI Era” (Gutegura impano z’ejo hazaza mu gihe cy’ubwenge buhangano).

Iyi nama yitabiriwe n'Umunyamabanga wa Leta muri Minisiteri y’Uburezi, Claudette Irere, hamwe n’abandi bafatanyabikorwa mu burezi baturutse muri ibyo bihugu byombi, baganira ku buryo bwo kwagura imikoreshereze ya AI mu mashuri, kungurana ubumenyi no kureba amahirwe y’ubufatanye mu kubaka uburezi bujyanye n'igihe.

Claudette Irere yagaragaje ko intego y’u Rwanda atari ugukoresha ikoranabuhanga ku bwaryo gusa, ahubwo ari ukureba ko rifasha kuzamura ireme ry’uburezi no gutuma abanyeshuri bose babona amahirwe angana yo kwiga.

Yagize ati: “Icyo dushyize imbere si ikoranabuhanga ku bwaryo, ahubwo ni ukureba ko ubwenge buhangano buzamura umusaruro w’uburezi kandi bugafasha abantu bose kubona amahirwe angana, abarimu bakaba ari bo shingiro ry’iri hinduka kandi bafite ubushobozi bukenewe.”

Ibi bigaragaza ko mu gihe AI igenda ihindura uburyo abantu biga, bakora ubushakashatsi kandi bakora imirimo itandukanye, abarimu bagomba guhabwa ubumenyi n'ibikoresho bibafasha gukoresha iryo koranabuhanga neza, badakuwe mu mwanya wabo w’ingenzi mu burezi.

Mu rwego rwo kwihutisha iterambere, u Rwanda rwamaze gushyiraho Politiki y’Igihugu y’Ubwenge Buhangano (National Artificial Intelligence Policy), igamije gukoresha AI mu guteza imbere ubukungu, kuzamura imibereho y’abaturage no kurushyira mu bihugu biyoboye udushya mu ikoranabuhanga rishingiye kuri AI.

Iyi politiki ifite intego yo guhindura u Rwanda ihuriro mpuzamahanga ry’ubushakashatsi n’udushya mu bwenge buhangano, ndetse no kurugira ihuriro ry’Afurika mu guteza imbere no gukoresha AI mu buryo burengera inyungu z’abantu bose.

Mu by’ingenzi igihugu cyiyemeje harimo kongerera abaturage ubumenyi bw’ikoranabuhanga, kubaka ubushobozi mu bushakashatsi, guteza imbere uburyo bwo kubika no guhererekanya amakuru mu mutekano, no gukoresha AI mu kunoza imitangire ya serivisi za Leta n’ibikorwa by’abikorera.

Mu rwego rw'uburezi, iyi ntego yatangiye gushyirwa mu bikorwa binyuze mu guhugura abarimu kugira ngo bashobore gukoresha AI mu myigishirize no gufasha abanyeshuri kubona ubumenyi bujyanye n'igihe.

U Rwanda kandi rwashyizeho ubufatanye n'ikigo Anthropic mu gihe cy'imyaka itatu, bugamije guteza imbere ikoreshwa rya AI mu nzego zirimo uburezi, ubuzima n'imikorere ya Leta.

Ibi kandi bigaragaza ko u Rwanda rukomeje gushaka abafatanyabikorwa bazarufasha kwihutisha ikoreshwa ry’ikoranabuhanga mu burezi no gutegura urubyiruko ruzagira uruhare mu bukungu bw’ejo hazaza.

Koreya y’Epfo ni kimwe mu bihugu byateye imbere mu ikoranabuhanga, ubushakashatsi n’inganda zigezweho. Kungurana ubumenyi na yo bishobora gufasha u Rwanda guteza imbere ubushobozi bw'abarimu, abanyeshuri n'abashakashatsi, ndetse no kwagura uburyo ikoranabuhanga rikoreshwa mu mashuri.

Icy'ingenzi muri ubu bufatanye ni uko AI itagomba gufatwa nk'ikoranabuhanga ryo gukuraho uruhare rw'umwarimu, ahubwo ikwiye kwifashiswa mu kunoza imyigishirize, gutahura aho umunyeshuri afite intege nke no kumufasha kubona ubufasha bujyanye n'ubushobozi bwe.

Uebert Angel is still in police custody following his arrest over the weekend

A well-known Zimbabwean preacher has been arrested on allegations of sexual offences, local police have said.

Uebert Angel, who leads an international charismatic church with branches around the world, was arrested during a church service in Harare on Sunday. Pictures and footage of the dramatic arrest have since been circulated online.

In one video, a convoy of vehicles is seen escorting the self-styled prophet as he sits in the back of a police van surrounded by armed police officers.

The controversial founder of Spirit Embassy was appointed Zimbabwe's special presidential envoy and ambassador-at-large to Europe and the Americas in 2021. He has not commented on the allegations.

In 2023, he made headlines when an undercover report by Al Jazeera claimed that he had offered to use his diplomatic status to launder large amounts of money through a gold-smuggling scheme in the country.

According to the Qatar-based network, Angel, 48, told reporters working undercover that the scheme was approved by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Zimbabwean police released a brief statement confirming his arrest on suspicion of indecent assault and sodomy. A member of his team told reporters the British-Zimbabwean national was still in police custody and it was unclear when he would appear in court.

"It can be in the afternoon or tomorrow [Tuesday]. We are still within the legal framework [for him to appear in court]," Professor Lovemore Madhuku told state-owned broadcaster ZBC in a clip posted online.

This is not the first time the prominent preacher has been accused of improper behaviour.

A report by local online publication ZimLIVE in 2021 said that Angel had previously faced allegations of sexual impropriety from several women, at least five of whom are in England. The charismatic preacher has denied the allegations, the outlet added at the time.

Angel's church has branches in Zimbabwe, South Africa and the UK and he is known for his ties to other prominent preachers like Malawian televangelist Shepherd Bushiri.
